name: UX Deliverables & Prototyping
description: The artifacts and tooling UX designers produce to communicate design intent and validate concepts. Covers process modeling deliverables (Customer Experience Map, Simple Flowchart, EPC, BPMN) and prototyping (wireframing tools, fidelity levels, and layout principles). These artifacts bridge research and production, enabling stakeholder alignment and usability testing.

subskills.name: Customer Experience Map
subskills.description: A visual artifact mapping the end-to-end customer journey across touchpoints, phases, actions, thoughts, emotions, and pain points. Differs from a user flow in that it captures the holistic experience including pre- and post-product touchpoints. Used to identify emotional peaks/valleys and moments of highest behavioral leverage.

subskills.name: Simple Flowchart
subskills.description: Basic process visualization using standard flowchart notation (start/end terminals, process boxes, decision diamonds, connectors). Used for communicating user flows, decision trees, and interaction paths at a level of simplicity accessible to all stakeholders including non-technical ones.

subskills.name: EPC — Event-Driven Process Chain
subskills.description: A formal process modeling notation used in enterprise UX and SAP-related contexts. EPC diagrams alternate Events (states) and Functions (activities), connected by logical operators (AND, OR, XOR). Used to model complex business processes with conditional paths and parallel flows.

subskills.name: BPMN — Business Process Model and Notation
subskills.description: The ISO-standardized notation for business process modeling. Covers BPMN 2.0 elements: pools, lanes, tasks, gateways (exclusive, parallel, inclusive), events (start, intermediate, end), and sequence flows. BPMN is the professional standard for communicating complex, multi-actor processes to both business and technical stakeholders.

subskills.name: Wireframing & Prototyping Tools
subskills.description: Proficiency in industry-standard wireframing and prototyping tools: Figma (the dominant collaborative design tool), Adobe XD, Sketch (macOS), and Balsamiq (low-fidelity rapid wireframing). Covers creating low-fidelity (lo-fi) sketches, mid-fidelity wireframes, and high-fidelity interactive prototypes. Also includes handoff workflows to engineering teams.

subskills.name: Good Layout Rules
subskills.description: Core visual design principles applied to UX layouts: visual hierarchy (F-pattern, Z-pattern reading), Gestalt principles (proximity, similarity, continuity, closure), grid systems (8-point grid, 12-column), white space, contrast ratios (WCAG 2.1 AA), typography scale, and responsive layout breakpoints.

junior.description: Creates lo-fi and mid-fi wireframes in Figma or equivalent, draws clear user flow diagrams, and applies grid systems and Gestalt principles in layouts.

mid.description: Produces comprehensive customer experience maps identifying emotional leverage points, and creates BPMN process models for multi-actor workflows.

senior.description: Models complex enterprise processes with EPC notation, establishes cross-team standards for UX deliverable formats, and governs design handoff quality.
